objective: Feasibility and topology audit for high-order mixed interfaces without creating a production workflow, changing FEM formulations, changing the 46-record maturity registry, or changing historical evidence.

scope.mechanics: No production static, modal, dynamic, contact, nonlinear, or public mixed high-order qualification is executed by WP13-09.

source_traceability.finding: All four element classes are individually registered; this does not establish mixed interface compatibility.
TET10 uses four corner nodes plus six midside edge nodes and validates the high-order geometry.
HEX20 uses eight corner nodes plus twelve midside edge nodes and validates sampled Jacobians.
High-order face definitions exist for TET10 and HEX20, but no WEDGE15 or PYRAMID13 topology exists.
Gmsh imports TET10/HEX20/WEDGE6/PYRAMID5 individually and maps high-order faces for surface targeting, but has no WEDGE15/PYRAMID13 transition mapping.
Mixed scope and face records enumerate TET4/WEDGE6/HEX8/PYRAMID5 only; TET10/HEX20 are not validated as mixed interface families.
Translation MPCs accept arbitrary linear coefficients, use affine elimination, expose rank/relation diagnostics, and recover constraint forces. No high-order face interpolator is provided.
RBE2 is expanded into translational linear MPC equations for its bounded route; it is not a high-order face transition generator.
The qualified MPC route is linear-static, conforming TET4/WEDGE6/HEX8, homogeneous and translational only; it excludes nonconforming interfaces and arbitrary MPCs.
PYRAMID5 feasibility is bounded to a HEX8/PYRAMID5/TET4 conforming patch and explicitly makes no PYRAMID13 or transition-mesh claim.

known_architecture_limits: TET10 and HEX20 are individually supported but their mixed high-order interface faces are not represented by the current mixed validator.
The current conforming interface model is exact shared node identity; a shared corner vertex set is insufficient when midside nodes are absent on the linear side.
Current MPC reduction can express linear interpolation equations but has no automatic face matching, curved-edge projection, transition-element generation, or high-order interface load audit.
WEDGE15 and PYRAMID13 are absent from the element registry and Gmsh family mapping.

WEDGE15.source: not present in current registry/topology/Gmsh mapping

PYRAMID13.source: not present in current registry/topology/Gmsh mapping

TET10_WEDGE6.reason: The TET10 face has three edge midside nodes absent from the WEDGE6 triangular face.

HEX20_WEDGE6.reason: The HEX20 face has four edge midside nodes absent from the WEDGE6 quadrilateral face.

TET10_TET4.reason: Shared corner nodes alone do not make a quadratic TRI6 trace conforming to TRI3.

HEX20_HEX8.reason: Shared corner nodes alone do not make a quadratic QUAD8 trace conforming to QUAD4.

TET10_PYRAMID5.reason: A PYRAMID5 triangular side is TRI3; PYRAMID5 does not supply the high-order face nodes.

HEX20_PYRAMID5.reason: A PYRAMID5 base is QUAD4; PYRAMID5 cannot connect a HEX20 QUAD8 trace directly.

WEDGE15.value: Would provide TRI6 and QUAD8 faces for high-order prism transitions.

PYRAMID13.value: Would provide high-order triangular and quadrilateral transition faces around a pyramid.

MPC_MIDSIDE_TYING.value: Can express bounded straight-interface relations u_mid = 0.5*(u_a + u_b), preserving affine traces but restricting the high-order interface to the linear neighbor space.
limitations: not automatically valid for curved midside geometry

HANGING_NODE_CONSTRAINTS.value: Could express p-transition constraints but no dedicated hanging-node topology/ownership path exists.

LOCAL_LINEAR_DOWNGRADE.value: A high-order element can be restricted at an interface to the linear trace, but this is a deliberate local p-downgrade and needs explicit transition semantics.

DEDICATED_TRANSITION_ELEMENT.value: The cleanest route for exact high-order continuity if the transition family and its shape functions are developed.

mcp_micro_spike.purpose: Pure algebraic feasibility check after contract freeze; not a production mixed FE campaign.

relations.triangle: For each translation component, each TRI6 midside node is constrained to the midpoint average of its two TRI3 corner nodes.
relations.quadrilateral: For each translation component, each QUAD8 edge node is constrained to the midpoint average of its two QUAD4 corner nodes.

required_checks: no overconstraint in the declared face-only system
constant translation and infinitesimal rotation preservation
zero resultant and zero moment of internal constraint-force pairs
stop_if: generalization beyond linear translation MPC is required
rank deficiency or redundant relation appears
rigid-body affine modes are not preserved
a full mechanics or production solver change is required

constraint_row_rank.definition: rank(C) equals the number of declared independent rows

rigid_mode_preservation.definition: max(abs(C u_rigid - d)) for three translations and three infinitesimal rotations

interface_continuity.definition: max displacement jump on shared face trace

load_transfer.definition: constraint-force resultant and moment pair residual for declared straight-face relations

determinism.definition: semantic digest of two identical algebraic constructions

topology_consistency.definition: face node counts and midside-node ownership match the declared topology matrix

oracle.primary: Independent algebraic construction of face interpolation matrix C from explicit corner/midside topology, compared against the production LinearConstraint/ConstraintReduction acceptance of the same declared relations.
oracle.independence_boundary: The check may call the existing generic validation/reduction primitives to test representability, but it must construct face relations independently and must not call a future high-order transition helper because none exists.
oracle.mechanical_oracle: NOT_RUN; WP13-09 is topology/feasibility only and does not qualify a static solve or interface mechanics.
oracle.shared_kernel_limitation: The algebraic check does not validate element K/M kernels, nonlinear geometry, contact, or external-solver correlation.

gmsh_reality.node_ordering_check: Use the existing TET10 Gmsh permutation and existing HEX20 Gmsh ordering; no transition ordering is available.
gmsh_reality.limitation: Gmsh can provide the endpoint families individually but the current importer has no native transition-element mapping or high-order/linear interface constraint generation.

decision_policy.case_2_TET10_HEX20_WEDGE6: NO_GO without an explicit transition mechanism; RESEARCH_ONLY with MPC or transition elements
decision_policy.case_3_high_order_linear_MPC: GO_WITH_LIMITATIONS only for bounded straight affine trace compatibility if all algebraic gates pass; not a production claim
decision_policy.case_4_transition_element: RESEARCH_ONLY until WEDGE15/PYRAMID13 or a dedicated transition element is implemented and independently qualified

evidence_schema.format: JSON manifest; arrays may be JSON lists; no production result archive is required

abort_criteria: contract is changed after the first micro-run
a production high-order mixed workflow is attempted
a numerical mechanics claim is inferred from the algebraic feasibility check
historical WP13-08, 0.2.7 evidence or maturity registry is modified
a silent family, node or constraint fallback is observed

claim_policy.maximum_claim: No public high-order mixed capability is created. At most, WP13-09 may document a bounded MPC transition feasibility direction for straight affine traces.
claim_policy.follow_up: A future implementation WP must predeclare a separate contract for geometry-aware transition relations or transition elements and perform full static V&V.
